Koda 0.1.4 provides guidance for avoiding the kind of scope mismatches that sometimes result in a fragment loading where it doesn't belong (such as in the main window). It also provides a way to display warnings that might help us figure out what went wrong. If we put
    somewhere on our page, the warnings will be displayed. For now, I propose adding it to our shell. I'm not sure if it also needs to be added in the design preview panel to catch errors there or not. I upgraded Prelude to use 0.1.4, but I'm guessing I'll need to do the same on the designed apps.

You're right on both counts: the preview needs its own list, and apps you've built need their own upgrade. But first, this checkout isn't running 0.1.4 yet. **Koda 0.1.2 is still installed here.** `package.json` and `package-lock.json` pin 0.1.4, but `node_modules/@kodalang/core/package.json` says `"version": "0.1.2"`. Prelude serves Koda from that folder (`/koda/` in `server/main.js:49,72`), so `
    ` would do nothing until `npm install` runs. Two other effects of the old copy: - The reference I can read is 0.1.2's. It mentions warnings only at `reference.md:358-360`, which describes Koda's own `console.warn`s. Nothing documents `ko-warnings`, so I can't confirm from the docs how it behaves. - The Build agent is told to pin the version that's installed (`server/agent.js:505`, from `kodaVersion` at `main.js:53`). Right now a newly built app would get 0.1.2. **The shell.** Prelude's real pages start Koda in `server/views/_regions.eta:51-54`, and the Prelude Shell design does the same in `prelude/prelude-shell/layouts/_regions.eta:45-46`. Put `
      ` in the design's layout and in the app's copy. That covers the problem you described, a fragment landing in the main window, because that happens in the app's own page. **The preview panel needs its own.** A design renders on a separate origin (`*.preview.localhost`, in `server/host.js`), as its own page that calls `start(document)` itself. Any warnings are raised in that page, so the shell's list in the outer window won't see them. The preview's page comes from one of three layouts: - the built-in `server/views/host/layout.eta`, used when a project has no shell; - the project's shell layouts. For Prelude's own designs that's the same `prelude/prelude-shell/layouts/_regions.eta`, so one edit covers the app and its previews; - layouts the agent writes. It follows the template in `server/agent.js:396`, so new shells won't include the list unless that template does. **Designed apps:** - **Previews** of any project's designs already load Prelude's Koda (`host.js:422`, `app.kodaDir`). They'll get 0.1.4 once it's installed here, with no change on their side. - **Built apps** pin their own Koda in their own `package.json`, and an `@app` view loads it from the app's own `/koda/` (`agent.js:476`). For each of those, bump the version and run `npm install` in that app's repository. For example, the borrower-portal snapshot in `prelude/build/snapshots/` loads its own `/koda/koda.js`. - OrchestratR doesn't use Koda at all, so it needs nothing. **What I'd change, on a branch:** 1. Run `npm install` here, then check 0.1.4's `docs/reference.md` for exactly what `ko-warnings` does. 2. In `prelude/prelude-shell/layouts/_regions.eta`, add `
        `, with a rule in `shell.css` to hide it while it's empty. Copy the same change into `server/views/_regions.eta`. 3. In `server/views/host/layout.eta`, add the same list, so projects without a shell get it too. 4. In `server/agent.js:396`, add the list to the layout template the agent writes shells from. 5. In each built app's repository, upgrade `@kodalang/core` to 0.1.4.

2150	
2151	| Attribute | Meaning |
2152	|---|---|
2153	| `ko-location` | The URL the region's current content came from. |
2154	| `ko-loading` | Present while a request for this region is in flight. |
2155	| `ko-selected` | On a matching `ko-marker`. |
2156	| `ko-unauthorized` | The application answered 401 - it could not tell who was asking. The region kept what it had; retry once signed in. |
2157	| `ko-can-back` | On a `ko-history="local"` element whose stack has somewhere to go back to. |
2158	| `ko-can-forward` | The same, forward. |
2159	
2160	## How a region gets its scope
2161	
2162	Explicit `ko-scope` wins. Otherwise the URL the region last loaded becomes its
2163	scope - so a panel that fetched `/orders/42` thereafter owns everything beneath
2164	`/orders/42`, and links inside it stay inside it. A region with neither owns
2165	nothing and can only be reached by `ko-target`.
2166	
2167	An inferred scope owns only what is beneath it: a panel showing `/orders/42`
2168	does not own `/orders/43`, so its own "next order" link goes to whatever owns
2169	`/orders`. And because an inferred scope follows the content, it also follows a
2170	redirect: a panel whose form at `/orders/new` redirected to `/orders/42` now
2171	owns `/orders/42`. When a region should own a URL space whatever it happens to
2172	be showing, say so with `ko-scope`.
2173	
2174	## Which region wins
2175	
2176	1. An explicit `ko-target` on the control, if it names a region. An optional
2177	   one (`drawer?`) that names nothing falls through to the next rule.
2178	2. Otherwise, of every region whose scope contains the URL: **the most specific
2179	   scope wins**, and nearest-in-the-tree breaks ties.
2180	3. If nothing owns the URL, Koda does not intervene and the browser navigates
2181	   normally.
2182	
2183	Rule 2 matters more than it looks. Taking the nearest match alone would hand a
2184	shell scoped to `/` every request on the page, including ones the panel next door
2185	exactly owns. Matc

With 0.1.4 installed I could read how `ko-warnings` works (`node_modules/@kodalang/core/docs/reference.md:2206-2251`, `src/dom/warnings.js`). It changes part of what I said before.

**What 0.1.4 does**
- The warning you want is `relocated-by-response`: an answer landed somewhere other than where its request was sent, such as a panel's redirect landing in `#main`. There's also `region-detached`, for an answer whose region was replaced while the request was out. Each warning is a sentence naming the scopes involved and the change that would keep the content in place.
- Koda only works out this advice if the page asks for it. The page asks either by containing a `[ko-warnings]` element or by calling `start` with `advise: true`. Koda checks for the element each time it warns (`warnings.js:41-43`), so an element added after `start(document)` still counts.
- Each warning is first sent as a `koda:warning` event, with `{ code, message, url, region, from }` in its `detail`. If nothing cancels the event, it's added to every `[ko-warnings]` list as an `<li ko-warning="code">`. With no list on the page, it goes to the console.
- The docs say a design tool or development host should provide the list, and "a production page simply does not have one".

That last point changes where the list belongs.

**Prelude's own shell: yes, as you proposed.** Prelude is a development tool, so a visible list there is fine. Put it in `prelude/prelude-shell/layouts/_regions.eta` and its app copy `server/views/_regions.eta`. That catches the main-window case in Prelude itself.

**The preview: yes, but have the preview server add it, not each shell.** Designs render in a frame, as their own page, so the shell's list never sees their warnings. Adding the list to each design's shell would be wrong: a design's shell layout becomes the built app's real layout, which production shouldn't have. Prelude already adds scripts to every preview page in one place:
- `withClient` in `server/host.js:507-510` inserts `CLIENT_SCRIPT` and `WHERE_SCRIPT`.
- `WHERE_SCRIPT` posts `prelude:where` to the design surface, which handles it in `server/views/_surface.eta:98`.

A third script added there could:
1. add a hidden `<ol ko-warnings>` to the body, which switches on the advice;
2. listen for `koda:warning`, cancel it, and post `{ type: 'prelude:warning', code, message, url }` to the parent. Only the strings, since an element can't be posted.

The design surface would then list them next to the preview. This covers every project's designs, and their shells need no change.

**Built apps:** these still need their own upgrade. Each one pins `@kodalang/core` in its own `package.json`, so bump it to 0.1.4 and run `npm install` in that app's repository. Leave the list out of their layouts. New apps will be pinned to 0.1.4, since Build pins the version Prelude has installed (`agent.js:505`).

**What I'd change, on a branch:**
1. **`prelude/prelude-shell/layouts/_regions.eta` and `server/views/_regions.eta`:** add `<ol ko-warnings>`, with styles in `shell.css` that place it and hide it while it's empty. Add a note in the shell's NOTES.md.
2. **`server/host.js`:** add a `WARNINGS_SCRIPT` next to `WHERE_SCRIPT`, inserted by `withClient`.
3. **`server/views/_surface.eta`:** handle `prelude:warning` and show the warnings, with a way to clear them. Record this in `prelude/design-workspace/NOTES.md`, next to `prelude:where` (around line 140).
4. **`server/agent.js:396`:** leave it as it is, so the shells the agent writes stay suitable for production.
5. **Each built app's repository:** upgrade `@kodalang/core` to 0.1.4.

4	what Prelude ships (`server/views/layout.eta`, the `.bar`/`.page`/`.workspace`
5	rules in `server/public/prelude.css`, and the pop-out `_window.eta`), on the

10	
11	- **app** - the bar, then the page scrolling with the window. Pages hold their

I've added Koda's warnings list to Prelude's shell, and the preview panel now sends a design page's warnings to that same list. I couldn't run anything, so none of it is tested yet.

**What was wrong:** No page asked Koda for the warnings, so a fragment landing in the wrong place went unreported. The preview couldn't be fixed through the shell: a design's page runs in a frame on its own origin and starts Koda itself, so a list in Prelude's own page never sees that page's warnings.

**What I changed:**
- **The shell:** `<ol id="warnings" ko-warnings>` is in `prelude/prelude-shell/layouts/_regions.eta` and the app's copy, `server/views/_regions.eta`. The styles are in both copies of `shell.css`. It sits at the bottom-left corner, opposite the notice, with a pale red background. It's hidden while empty and has a Clear button.
- **The preview:** `server/host.js` now adds a small script (`WARNINGS_SCRIPT`) to every design page shown in the frame:
  - If the page has no warnings list, it adds a hidden one. That's what turns Koda's advice on.
  - It catches each warning and sends it to the preview panel around the frame.
  - `server/views/_surface.eta` adds each one to the shell's list, starting "In the design's page: …".
  
  This covers every project's designs, and no design's layouts need a list. Those layouts become real apps' layouts, which shouldn't show one.
- **Unchanged:** the shell template Prelude's agent writes for other projects (`server/agent.js`), for the same reason.
- **Notes:** I added a line to each of the two designs' NOTES.md and wrote the fix's NOTES.md.

**To run:** `node --test test/host.test.js`, which has a new test that the framed page gets the script and the panel listens for its warnings, then `npm test`.

**To check:**
- **Your shell:** to see the list appear, run this in your console, then check that Clear hides it again:
  ```js
  document.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('koda:warning', { bubbles: true, cancelable: true, detail: { code: 'test', message: 'hello' } }))
  ```
- **The preview:** run the same line in the frame's console. The warning should appear in Prelude's list, starting "In the design's page".
- **The look:** I chose the bottom-left corner and the pale red background myself. If you'd like it placed or styled differently, that can go to a design session.

**Apps you've already built** each pin their own copy of Koda. In each app's repository, change `@kodalang/core` to `0.1.4` in `package.json` and run `npm install`. New builds will get 0.1.4 automatically, because Build uses the version Prelude has installed.
